Estimate a Network (Deprecated)

Source: R/estimate_network.R
estimate_network.Rd

estimate_network() is deprecated: use build_network() instead. It passes its arguments to build_network() unchanged and returns what that returns, after a warning of class deprecatedWarning.

Usage

estimate_network(
  data,
  method = "relative",
  params = list(),
  scaling = NULL,
  threshold = 0,
  level = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

The data to estimate from: a data frame of sequences (one row per sequence, one column per position), an event log (one row per event, with action set), one-hot code columns, numeric variables (one row per observation) for the association methods, or a square symmetric correlation or covariance matrix. A fitted net_clustering or net_mmm object also works: its per-cluster networks are built, with the scaling, threshold, start, end and params given here, and returned as a netobject_group. The relative networks of a net_mmm are the fitted chains: scaling and threshold are applied to them, and any other argument raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

method

The estimator, as in build_network(). Default "relative", kept for backward compatibility; build_network() has no default.

params

Settings passed to the estimator, as a named list, such as list(gamma = 0.5) for glasso or list(n_gram = 3) for ngram. The list is stored on the network, so bootstrap_network() and the other resampling verbs re-estimate with exactly the same settings. The transition methods take tna's sequence options weighted and concat, and the low-level begin_state / end_state that start and end set. window_size (with window_span, or windowed = TRUE for a size of 2) counts relative, frequency and co_occurrence between consecutive non-overlapping blocks of that many positions, as tna::tna() does; other transition methods raise an error of class nestimate_bad_input, and mode = "overlapping" a warning of class nestimate_ignored_mode. Column roles given here (action, id, id_col, actor, time, session, order, cols, codes, group) must name existing columns, and must agree with the same role given directly.

scaling

Rescaling applied to the weights after estimation, in the order given: "minmax" maps the non-zero weights into (0, 1], "max" divides by the largest absolute weight, "rank" replaces the non-zero weights by their ranks, and "normalize" makes each row's absolute weights sum to 1. Zero weights stay zero under every option. Combine them as in c("rank", "minmax"). Default NULL (none).

threshold

Weights whose absolute value is below this are set to zero. Default 0 (none). For method = "mgm", "LW" or "none" instead selects mgm's coefficient-thresholding rule (a threshold in params takes precedence); any other non-numeric value raises an error.

level

Multilevel decomposition for the undirected association methods (cor, pcor, glasso, mgm): "between" estimates the network of person means, "within" the network of deviations from them, and "both" returns the two as a netobject_ml. It needs an id column, given as actor or as params$id; a directed method raises an error. Default NULL (no decomposition). For method = "mgm", a numeric vector instead gives one category count per modelled variable (1 for continuous ones), after group, actor and metadata columns are set aside; it is checked and kept for compatibility, and the fit reads the categories from the data.

...

Further arguments for build_network(), such as actor, action, time or group.

Value

A netobject, exactly as build_network() returns it (a netobject_group or netobject_ml when ... or level asks for one).

See also

build_network

Examples

data <- data.frame(T1 = c("x","y","z","x"), T2 = c("y","x","z","y"))
net <- estimate_network(data, method = "relative")
#> Warning: 'estimate_network' is deprecated.
#> Use 'build_network' instead.
#> See help("Deprecated")
